objectives: Hear and identify /f/ in spoken words.
Identify /f/ in initial and final positions.
Prepare for /f/ grapheme connection and decoding.
concepts: /f/ can occur at the beginning or end of a word.
Sound discrimination supports later grapheme mapping and decoding.

definitions.definition: The smallest unit of sound that can distinguish words.
The ability to notice whether spoken sounds are the same or different.
The first sound heard in a spoken word.
The last sound heard in a spoken word.

commonMistakes: Focusing on the letter name instead of the speech sound.

basic: Repeat /f/ and identify it in familiar spoken words.
application: Sort spoken words by /f/ position and identify contrasts.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why sound discrimination comes before grapheme decoding.
mixedReview: Mix initial and final /f/ identification with known sounds.

formulaOrFactBank: Initial position = first sound; final position = last sound.
mistakeBasedRevision: If /f/ is confused with another sound, use minimal oral contrasts before print.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat spoken /f/ sorting with fresh words until accuracy is stable.

activities.name: Sound sort
steps: Say one word at a time.

activities.name: Position check
steps: Use words with /f/ initially and finally.

activities.name: Contrast practice
steps: Ask learner to identify the first sound.

outcomes: Learner identifies /f/ in new spoken words.
Learner is ready to connect /f/ to print.
